quizName: DMV Practice Test #6 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen:

options.text: On short trips.
On long trips.
After at least an hour of riding.
After more than 8 hours of riding.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on trips less than five miles long, within a few minutes of starting to ride.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: Where is the engine cut-off switch usually located?

options.text: Near the left handgrip
Near the right handgrip
Near the left footrest
Near the right footrest

questions.explanation: The engine cut-off switch is located next to the right handgrip. Know where all your motorcycle's controls are before you start riding.

questions.question: It is important to flash your brake light when:

options.text: Approaching a police officer.
Someone is following too closely.
There is a stop sign ahead.
Your signals are not working.

questions.explanation: Flash your brake light before slowing down if someone is following too closely. This alerts the driver that you are slowing down, especially if they may not see the hazard ahead that is making you slow.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection, you should:

options.text: Ride in the portion of the lane that will bring you into other drivers' fields of vision at the earliest possible moment.
Always be in the left lane to be the farthest from oncoming traffic.
Slowly sneak up to the intersection.
Weave slightly in your lane so your headlight has a better chance of being spotted.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the portion of the lane that will bring you into other drivers' fields of vision at the earliest possible moment.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection, position yourself in the lane so oncoming drivers can see you as soon as possible. For example, when approaching a blind corner to your right, ride on the left side of your lane so you are visible sooner.

questions.question: To lessen your chances of an accident, you should:

options.text: Only ride in the afternoon.
Follow the vehicle in front of you as closely as possible.
Not look ahead and focus only on your controls.
Communicate your intentions to other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Communicate your intentions to other drivers.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make sure other drivers can see you. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position to tell them what you are doing. Keep space around your motorcycle and watch the road ahead, behind, and to the sides.

questions.question: A group of riders should pass another vehicle:

options.text: In a staggered formation.
In a pyramid formation.
One at a time.
In a splintered formation.

questions.explanation: On a two-lane highway, riders should pass one at a time. The second rider waits until the first rider safely returns to the original lane before passing. Riders continue this pattern until all have passed the vehicle.

questions.question: When preparing to pass another vehicle on the left, you should:

options.text: Ride in the right portion of the lane.
Ride in the left portion of the lane.
Get as close as possible to the vehicle in front of you.
Not signal your intentions, as that may distract the driver you are passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the left portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When passing on the left, ride in the left portion of your lane. Signal your intentions and check for traffic. Pass when it is safe, then signal and return to your original lane.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Is not necessary if you have a windshield.
Only protects your eyes.
Helps protect your whole face.
Does not protect your face as well as goggles.

questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your whole face in a crash. Goggles protect only your eyes. A windshield is not a replacement for a face shield or goggles.

questions.question: How often should a motorcycle operator check their mirrors?

options.text: Never
Occasionally
Frequently
More often than the amount time spent looking ahead

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors frequently to be aware of hazards behind you.

questions.question: What should you do if your motorcycle starts to wobble?

options.text: Speed up to get out of the wobble.
Use the brakes slowly.
Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly release the throttle.
Shift to a lower gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly release the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up when your motorcycle wobbles. Instead, hold the handlebars firmly without fighting the wobble. Slowly release the throttle to slow down. Lean your weight forward and down. Pull off the road as soon as you can.

questions.question: Riders without helmets are ________ to die in a crash than riders with helmets.

options.text: Half as likely
Twice as likely
Three times as likely
Just as likely

questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries in a crash than riders with helmets, no matter what speed you are going.

questions.question: What does reflective material on your helmet do?

options.text: Helps other drivers see you.
Is not allowed.
Should only be used at night.
Does not help you be seen.

questions.explanation: Reflective material on your vest or helmet sides makes you more visible to other drivers. Use it both day and night.

questions.question: Where should you ride to be seen in the rearview mirror of the car ahead?

options.text: In the center of your lane.
In the left side of your lane.
In the right side of your lane.
In a weaving pattern.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane behind a car. This places you in the driver's rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirror much more often than their side mirrors.

questions.question: Most motorcycles have:

options.text: Only a front brake.
Only a rear brake.
A front brake and a rear brake.
Three brakes: front, rear, and emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: A front brake and a rear brake.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have two brakes: one for the front wheel and one for the rear wheel.

questions.question: When braking, what should you do?

options.text: Squeeze the front brake and press the rear brake.
Grab the front brake and squeeze the rear brake.
Jam the front brake and grab the rear brake.
Press the front brake and jam the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Squeeze the front brake and press the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Squeeze the front brake lever and press down on the rear brake pedal. Always use both brakes when slowing or stopping.

questions.question: How do you lean your motorcycle for a turn?

options.text: Press the handgrip toward the turn.
Press the handgrip away from the turn.
Apply the front brake.
Apply the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip toward the turn.
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle must lean to turn. Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn to make this happen.

questions.question: For regular braking, what should you do?

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use only the rear brake.
Switch between front and rear brakes to make them last longer.
Use both the front and rear brakes together.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes together.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding, what is usually the best thing to do?

options.text: Relax your grip on the handlebars.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Use the good tire's brake and steer to the side of the road.
Use both brakes and stop quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the good tire's brake and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: Hold the handlebars firmly and slow down by easing off the throttle. Keep going straight. If you must brake, slowly use the brake of the tire that is still good. Move toward the side of the road as you slow down. Squeeze the clutch and stop.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, what should you do?

options.text: Stay in a position where the driver can see you.
Always ride in the far left of your lane.
Do not worry about your position.
Always ride in the far right of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in a position where the driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane behind a car. The driver is most likely to see you in their rearview mirror from this position. Drivers check their rearview mirror much more often than their side mirrors.

questions.question: When using a sidecar to carry a load, what should you do?

options.text: Let the load move freely.
Secure the load so it does not shift.
Place the load unsecured in the seat.
Secure the load near the front of the sidecar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secure the load so it does not shift.
questions.explanation: A shifting load can affect how your motorcycle handles. Keep the load toward the rear of the sidecar to prevent the nose from tipping up during sharp left turns.

questions.question: As a new rider, what following distance should you keep behind other vehicles?

options.text: At least four seconds behind.
As close as possible to the other vehicle.
You do not need to worry about following distance.
Always ride on the left side of the lane so drivers can see you.

questions.explanation: New riders should stay at least four seconds behind the vehicle in front of them. Increase this distance if conditions are poor, like rain or fog.

questions.question: Where do most conflicts happen between motorcycles and other vehicles?

options.text: Intersections
Highways
Parking lots
Residential areas

questions.explanation: Most conflicts happen at intersections, where other vehicles may cross your path. Stay extra alert at these locations.

questions.question: A person is legally considered intoxicated if their blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is at least ______.

options.text: 0.02 percent
0.04 percent
0.08 percent
0.1 percent

questions.explanation: In Kentucky, a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is legally intoxicated. Never operate a motorcycle while under the influence of alcohol.

questions.question: After mounting your motorcycle, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Check that the mirrors are clean.
Test that the horn works.
Close the fuel supply valve.
Check that the clutch works smoothly.

questions.explanation: Before riding, check the clutch, throttle, horn, and brakes. Clean the mirrors. Keep the fuel supply valve open so gas can reach the engine.
